title: CFPB Ordered Cash App Parent Block to Pay Up to $175 Million
alt_title_1: Why Cash App's Support Number Sent Fraud Victims to Voicemail
alt_title_2: Inside the $175M CFPB Order Over Cash App Fraud Disputes
description_hook: In Consent Order 2025-CFPB-0001, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ordered Cash App parent Block, Inc. to pay up to $120 million in consumer redress plus a $55 million civil penalty over fraud-investigation and customer-support failures. Block consented without admitting or denying the findings.

affiliate_cta.offer_name: Free 48-Case Lawsuit & Refund Dossier + Forensics Reading List
affiliate_cta.pinned_comment: Do you keep a cash balance sitting inside peer-to-peer payment apps? Full CFPB Consent Order PDF is linked in the description.

scenes.headline: Card Line Played a Recording
scenes.narration: Until 2021, Cash App's card support line played a recording instead of answering fraud victims.

scenes.headline: Challenged 75% of Chargebacks
scenes.narration: When victims asked banks to reverse unauthorized transfers, Block challenged at least 75 percent of chargebacks.

scenes.headline: Up to $120M Back to Users
scenes.narration: The CFPB ordered up to 120 million dollars in user refunds plus a 55 million penalty.

scenes.headline: $175M CFPB Order on Block
scenes.narration: Without admitting or denying the findings, Cash App parent Block consented to provide live phone support.
scenes.source: In the Matter of Block, Inc., 2025-CFPB-0001, p. 1 (Jan 16, 2025)

scenes.headline: Apps Are Wallets, Not Vaults
scenes.right_body: Keep real savings off P2P apps
scenes.narration: Treat payment apps like a pocket wallet. Sweep spare cash straight back to an insured bank.
